context.title: Those Who Came Home
context.summary: After stating that Judah was exiled for unfaithfulness, the Chronicler lists those who resettled Jerusalem — laypeople, priests, Levites and gatekeepers — and describes the gatekeepers' duties.
context.background: This list closely parallels Nehemiah 11 and describes the community after the return. Settlers came from Judah and Benjamin but also from Ephraim and Manasseh (v. 3), supporting the book's theme of 'all Israel.' Saul's family is repeated at the end to lead into chapter 10.

customs.note: Literally 'given ones' — temple servants who assisted the Levites.
Gatekeepers, not baggage carriers. They guarded the gates, storerooms and treasures and opened the temple each morning.

watchFor: The chapter begins with the reason for exile: 'their transgression' (v. 1).
Singers were on duty 'day and night' (v. 33).

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

people.name: Pharez
people.summary: Pharez,, breach, the son of Judah (Neh. 11:4). “The chief of all the captains of the host for the first month” in the reign of David was taken from his family (1 Chr. 27:3).

people.name: Ammihud
people.summary: The son of Omri, and the father of Uthai (1 Chr. 9:4).

people.name: Bani
people.summary: Son of Imri.

people.name: Imri
people.summary: Of the Judah Tribe.

people.name: Uthai
people.summary: Son of Ammihud.

people.name: Asaiah
people.summary: Sons.In Context.

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: A son of Tamar (Gen. 38:30); called also Zara (Matt. 1:3).

people.name: Jeuel
people.summary: Snatched away by God, a descendant of Zerah (1 Chr. 9:6).

people.name: Hasenuah
people.summary: Bristling or hated, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 9:7).

people.name: Hodaviah
people.summary: Of the Benjamites.

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: Son of Has-senuah.

people.name: Sallu
people.summary: A Benjamite living in Jerusalem.

people.name: Elah
people.summary: Chief.

people.name: Jeroham
people.summary: 1 Chr. 9:8; a Benjamite.

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: Tribe of Benjamin.

people.name: Michri
people.summary: Prize of Jehovah, a Benjamite, the father of Uzzi (1 Chr. 9:8).

people.name: Uzzi
people.summary: A Benjamite, a chief in the tribe (1 Chr. 9:8).

people.name: Jedaiah
people.summary: A priest in Jerusalem after the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

people.name: Joiarib
people.summary: The founder of one of the courses of the priests (Neh. 11:10).

people.name: Jachin
people.summary: One of the priests who returned from the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

people.name: Hilkiah
people.summary: The high priest in the reign of Josiah (1 Chr. 6:13; Ezra 7:1). To him and his deputy (2 Kings 23:5), along with the ordinary priests and the Levites who had charge of the gates, was entrusted the purification of the temple in Jerusalem.

people.name: Meraioth
people.summary: Father of Amariah, a high priest of the line of Eleazar (1 Chr. 6:6, 7, 52).

people.name: Shallum
people.summary: Son of Zadok.

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: Father of Johanan.

people.name: Zadok
people.summary: The Priest.

people.name: Pashur
people.summary: Son of Malchiah.

people.name: Adaiah
people.summary: Priest resettling Jerusalem.

people.name: Azareel
people.summary: A priest (1 Chr. 9:12).

people.name: Immer
people.summary: Son of Meshullam.

people.name: Jeroham
people.summary: 1 Chr. 9:12; a priest, perhaps the same as in Neh. 11:12.

people.name: Maasiai
people.summary: Work of Jehovah, one of the priests resident at Jerusalem at the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:12).

people.name: Malchijah
people.summary: The first Malchijah mentioned in the Bible was a priest of ancient Israel after the order of Aaron, during the reign of King David in the 10th century BC. Malchijah led the fifth of the 24 priestly divisions. The biblical passage of 1 Chronicles 24 documents the division of the priests during the reign of King David. These priests were all descendants of Aaron, who had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. However, Nadab and Abihu died before Aaron and only Eleazar and Ithamar had sons. One priest, Zadok, from Eleazar's descendants and another priest, Ahimelech, from Ithamar's descendants were designated to help create the various priestly orders. Sixteen of Eleazar's descendants were selected to head priestly orders while only eight of Ithamar's descendants were so chosen. The passage states that this was done because of the greater number of leaders among Eleazar's descendants. Lots were drawn to designate the order of ministering for the heads of the priestly orders when they entered the temple. Since each order was responsible for ministering during a different week, Malchijah's order was stationed as a watch at the Tabernacle during the fifth week of the year on the Hebrew calendar.

people.name: Meshillemith
people.summary: A priest, the son of Immer (Neh. 11:13).

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: A priest (1 Chr. 9:12).

people.name: Jahzerah
people.summary: Returner, the son of Meshullam, and father of Adiel (1 Chr. 9:12).

people.name: Merari
people.summary: Sad; bitter, the youngest son of Levi, born before the descent of Jacob into Egypt, and one of the seventy who accompanied him thither (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16).

people.name: Azrikam
people.summary: Father of Hasshub.

people.name: Hashabiah
people.summary: One of the Levite leaders in the time of Ezra.

people.name: Hasshub
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (Neh. 11:15; 1 Chr. 9:14).

people.name: Asaph
people.summary: Son of Mika.

people.name: Micha
people.summary: The son of Zabdi, a Levite of the family of Asaph (Neh. 11:17, 22).

people.name: Zichri
people.summary: A Levite, one of the sons of Asaph (Neh. 11:17); probably the same as Zichri (1 Chr. 9:15), and Zaccur (Neh. 12:35).

people.name: Obadiah
people.summary: A Levite, after the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:16).

people.name: Galal
people.summary: Son ofJeduthun.

people.name: Jeduthun
people.summary: The King's Seer.

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: A Levite (1 Chr. 9:16).

people.name: Asa
people.summary: Who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.

people.name: Berechiah
people.summary: Levite resettler of Jerusalem.

people.name: Elkanah
people.summary: Of the Levites.

people.name: Akkub
people.summary: A Levite who kept the gate of the temple after the return from Babylon (1 Chr. 9:17; Ezra 2:42; Neh. 7:45).

people.name: Shallum
people.summary: A keeper of the gate in the reign of David (1 Chr. 9:17).

people.name: Talmon
people.summary: A Levite porter (1 Chr. 9:17; Neh. 11:19).

people.name: Ahiman
people.summary: One of the guardians of the temple after the Exile (1 Chr. 9:17).

people.name: Levi
people.summary: The third son of Jacob by Leah. The origin of the name is found in Leah’s words (Gen. 29:34), “This time will my husband be joined [Heb. yillaveh] unto me.”

people.name: Korah
people.summary: A Levite, the son of Izhar, the brother of Amram, the father of Moses and Aaron (Ex. 6:21). The institution of the Aaronic priesthood and the Levitical service at Sinai was a great religious revolution.

people.name: Ebiasaph
people.summary: Father of gathering; the gatherer, the youngest of the three sons of Korah the Levite, head of a family of Korhites (Ex. 6:24); called Ebisaph (1 Chr. 6:37).

people.name: Kore
people.summary: A Levite and temple-warder of the Korahites, the son of Asaph.

people.name: Eleazar
people.summary: The third son of Aaron (Ex. 6:23). His wife, a daughter of Putiel, bore him Phinehas (Ex. 6:25). After the death of Nadab and Abihu (Lev. 10:12; Num. 3:4) he was appointed to the charge of the sanctuary (Num. 3:32).

people.name: Phinehas
people.summary: Son of Eleazar, the high priest (Ex. 6:25). While yet a youth he distinguished himself at Shittim by his zeal against the immorality into which the Moabites had tempted the people (Num. 25:1-9), and thus “stayed the plague” that had broken out among the people, and by which twenty-four thousand of them perished.

people.name: Zechariah
people.summary: A Levite who assisted at the bringing up of the ark from the house of Obededom (1 Chr. 15:20-24).

people.name: Meshelemiah
people.summary: Friendship of Jehovah, a Levite of the family of the Korhites, called also Shelemiah (1 Chr. 9:21; 26:1, 2, 9, 14).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Samuel
people.summary: Heard of God. The peculiar circumstances connected with his birth are recorded in 1 Sam. 1:20. Hannah, one of the two wives of Elkanah, who came up to Shiloh to worship before the Lord, earnestly prayed to God that she might become the mother of a son.

people.name: Mattithiah
people.summary: The eldest son of Shallum, of the family of Korah (1 Chr. 9:31).

people.name: Abiel
people.summary: The son of Zeror and father of Ner, who was the grandfather of Saul (1 Sam. 14:51; 1 Chr. 8:33; 9:39).

people.name: Maachah
people.summary: Wife of David.

people.name: Ner
people.summary: Light, the father of Kish (1 Chr. 8:33). 1 Sam. 14:51 should be read, “Kish, the father of Saul, and Ner, the father of Abner, were the sons of Abiel.”

people.name: Kish
people.summary: A Benjamite, the son of Abiel, and father of king Saul (1 Sam. 9:1, 3; 10:11, 21; 14:51; 2 Sam. 21:14). All that is recorded of him is that he sent his son Saul in search of his asses that had strayed, and that he was buried in Zelah.

people.name: Abdon
people.summary: The first-born of Gibeon of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:30; 9:36).

people.name: Baal
people.summary: A Benjamite, son of Jehiel, the progenitor of the Gibeonites (1 Chr. 8:30; 9:36).

people.name: Nadab
people.summary: Son of Abiel.

people.name: Zur
people.summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:30).

people.name: Mikloth
people.summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:32; 9:37, 38).

people.name: Ahio
people.summary: One of the sons of Jehiel the Gibeonite (1 Chr. 8:31; 9:37).

people.name: Zacher
people.summary: Memorial, a son of Jehiel (1 Chr. 8:31; 9:35); called Zechariah (9:37).

people.name: Jonathan
people.summary: The eldest son of king Saul, and the bosom friend of David. He is first mentioned when he was about thirty years of age, some time after his father’s accession to the throne (1 Sam. 13:2).

people.name: Abinadab
people.summary: One of Saul’s sons, who peristed with his father in the battle of Gilboa (1 Sam. 31:2; 1 Chr. 10:2).

people.name: Malchi-shua
people.summary: King of help, one of the four sons of Saul (1 Chr. 8:33).

people.name: Mephibosheth
people.summary: The son of Jonathan, and grandson of Saul (2 Sam. 4:4). He was but five years old when his father and grandfather fell on Mount Gilboa. The child’s nurse hearing of this calamity, fled with him from Gibeah, the royal residence, and stumbling in her haste, the child was thrown to the ground and maimed in both his feet, and ever after was unable to walk (19:26).

people.name: Micah
people.summary: The son of Merib-baal (Mephibosheth), 1 Chr. 8:34, 35.

people.name: Ahaz
people.summary: A grandson of Jonathan (1 Chr. 8:35; 9:42).

people.name: Melech
people.summary: King, the second of Micah’s four sons (1 Chr. 8:35), and thus grandson of Mephibosheth.

people.name: Moza
people.summary: The son of Zimri, of the posterity of Saul (1 Chr. 8:36, 37; 9:42, 43).

people.name: Alemeth
people.summary: One of the sons of Jehoadah, or Jarah, son of Ahaz (1 Chr. 8:36).

people.name: Azel
people.summary: Noble, a descendant of king Saul (1 Chr. 8:37; 9:43, 44).

people.name: Eleasah
people.summary: A descendant of king Saul (1 Chr. 8:37; 9:43).

people.name: Rephaiah
people.summary: Binea.

people.name: Hanan
people.summary: A descendant of Saul (1 Chr. 8:38).

people.name: Ishmael
people.summary: Ishmael is the figure known in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam as Abraham's son, born to Haga.

people.name: Obadiah
people.summary: A descendant of Saul (1 Chr. 8:38).

places.name: Babylon
places.summary: The Greek form of BABEL; Semitic form Babilu, meaning “The Gate of God.” In the Assyrian tablets it means “The city of the dispersion of the tribes.”

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Gibeon
places.summary: Hill-city, “one of the royal cities, greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty” (Josh. 10:2). Its inhabitants were Hivites (11:19).
